text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A randomized trial in obese women found that intermittent fasting combined with calorie restriction reduced body weight, fat mass and visceral fat.","cited_pids":["23334c40ad6b#0","23334c40ad6b#1"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"In that obese women trial, a liquid-diet arm lost more weight than the other arms.","cited_pids":["23334c40ad6b#0","23334c40ad6b#1"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"A high-protein intermittent-fasting, low-calorie diet produced weight loss and improved arterial function in obese adults.","cited_pids":["c74e11d8769a#0"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"A meta-analysis of randomized trials found intermittent energy restriction comparable to continuous energy restriction for weight loss and cardiometabolic outcomes.","cited_pids":["e5aee0e45fc5#0","ebc373b389d7#0"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Harvard's Nutrition Source reports a randomized trial of 100 obese individuals over one year found intermittent fasting no more effective than daily calorie restriction.","cited_pids":["44e3472ec92d#7"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"A Cochrane review of 22 trials found intermittent fasting produced no significantly greater weight loss than standard diet advice.","cited_pids":["5a896703f2e3#0"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"Intermittent fasting works mainly as a calorie-reduction method, with weight loss similar to standard dieting rather than superior.","cited_pids":[]},{"cid":"c8","text":"The evidence on intermittent fasting for weight loss is of moderate confidence because trials are mixed and small.","cited_pids":[]}]}
